_about: Public-domain Nicolas Caussin (1583-1651), Jesuit confessor to Louis XIII, for the Word Hoard: The Holy Court in Sir T. H.'s translation (1634, 1638, and the five-tome third edition of 1663), The Christian Diary (Cambridge, 1648) and the Entertainments for Lent translated by Sir Basil Brook (Liverpool, 1755), from Internet Archive scans of the early printed books. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 37 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

caussin-holy-court-1634: The Holy Court in Three Tomes, tr. Sir T. H. (John Cousturier, M.DC.XXXIIII)
caussin-holy-court-passions-1638: The Holy Court: The Command of Reason over the Passions, tr. Sir T. H. (M.DC.XXXVIII)
caussin-holy-court-1663: The Holy Court in Five Tomes, the third edition, tr. Sir T. H. and others (London: for John Williams, MDCLXIII)
caussin-entertainments-lent-1755: Entertainments for Lent, by Sir Basil Brook (Liverpool: John Sadler, M.DCC.LV)

_alternates.caussin-copies: The Holy Court 1626 (title page illegible) and 1664; The Christian Diary 1652; The Christian Diurnal 1686; Entertainments for Lent 1661; The Unfortunate Politique 1653 (translators not legible)

_excluded.caussin-other: The Holy History (1653): the title page shows it is Nicolas Talon's; a modern machine translation of De Eloquentia catalogued 1627
